audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Warwick six of seven rows; the already-audited mirror (chogath__warwick) settled it as Skill / Warwick / Warwick / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath with ratings 5,4,4,6,7,7,7.
audit.why: The two directions must not contradict, and mirror-fix.js would overwrite a disagreement anyway. The mirror's reasoning holds up against the kits: Rupture cancels a 110s channel and Feral Scream silences the Q, both of which get worse for Warwick as ranks go in.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 3-6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group; ratings set to the inverse of the mirror's (5,6,6,4,3,3,3). whys[0], whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] rewritten to the side they now hold.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text had no cooldowns and claimed a '1.5s wind-up' on Rupture that is not in the kit data.
audit.why: Rupture's cast delay is not in Riot's description, so it cannot be asserted. Its 6s flat cooldown is, and so is Feral Scream's 11s and Infinite Duress' 110s.
audit.corrected: Unverifiable wind-up removed; Rupture's flat 6s, Feral Scream's 11s and Infinite Duress' 110s written into spikes[0], spikes[1] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike said to 'ult him through Rupture and Silence (W)' — the exact opposite of what those abilities do. Infinite Duress is a channel: Rupture's knockup cancels it, and Feral Scream's silence denies the cast outright. The late text also called Warwick's R an 'execute' and treated Feast stacking as a wall he cannot get through.
audit.why: Warwick's R carries the channel flag (any CC cancels it) and has no execute component. Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on the target's MAXIMUM health — so Feast stacking makes the Q hit harder, not softer. The mirror flagged this same inversion as the most dangerous claim on the Cho'Gath page.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] rewritten to say leap only after Rupture and Feral Scream are spent; late and spikes[3] rewritten to state that Feast stacks feed your max-health Q and that Feral Scream, not the health pool, is what stops you.

edits.before: Level 1 you dominate — Cho'Gath has no early trade pattern to answer your Q sustain and Blood Hunt pressure.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — Carnivore keeps him topped up off kills, and Blood Hunt does nothing at full health.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are even — his Vorpal Spikes wave-clear and your sustain trade blows without a clear edge.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 go to Cho'Gath — Feral Scream silences Jaws of the Beast and Vorpal Spikes chips you.

edits.before: Level 6 is yours: Infinite Duress locks and bursts him before Feast is a real threat.
edits.after: Level 6 is his: Rupture cancels a 110s Infinite Duress and Feast is true damage.

edits.before: At first item you still out-sustain a low-stack Cho'Gath in extended fights.
edits.after: At first item his stacked health blunts you and Feral Scream cuts trades.

edits.before: With Q's heal and Blood Hunt speed you win extended trades before Cho'Gath stacks Vorpal Spikes; bait his Rupture (Q) then walk in during its 1.5s wind-up and Jaws him while he's on cooldown.
edits.after: With Jaws of the Beast healing you and Blood Hunt speeding you at a low target, you win extended trades before Vorpal Spikes stack; bait Rupture — a flat 6s — then step in while it is down.

edits.before: Your Infinite Duress arrives before his Feast threat scales; ult him through Rupture and Silence (W) to burst him before he can Feast-execute you back.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a 110s channel — Rupture's knockup cancels it and Feral Scream denies the cast. Leap only once both are spent, never straight into his face.

edits.before: Once Cho'Gath has Feast stacks and health he becomes a wall you can't execute; his true-damage Feast and W silence flip the extended fight against your dive.
edits.after: Feast stacks make him tanky, not immune — Jaws of the Beast scales on max health, so it hits harder every stack. Feral Scream is what actually stops the dive.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 favour you: dodge his telegraphed Rupture (Q), close with Blood Hunt, and use Q's heal to win the return trade before Vorpal Spikes chunk you. At 6 your Infinite Duress can lock and burst him faster than he can Feast.
edits.after: Level 3 is yours: dodge the telegraphed Rupture and use Jaws of the Beast to win the return trade. From 4 it turns — Feral Scream silences your Q mid-trade on an 11s cooldown, and Rupture cancels Infinite Duress outright, so leap from his flank.

edits.before: By first and second item the matchup tips to Cho'Gath — Feast stacks give him a health pool your execute can't finish, and a well-timed W silence cancels your Q and ult mid-dive. Play for early leads and side-lane pressure before he walls up.
edits.after: By first item the matchup tips to Cho'Gath — but Feast stacking is not the wall it looks like: Jaws of the Beast deals max-health damage, so every stack feeds your Q. His real answer is Feral Scream, which silences it mid-dive. Take early leads.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Cho'Gath's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a directional leap and a channel — Rupture's knockup cancels it outright. Feast is true damage, so never brawl him low at 6.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool — build your teamfight around that. Cho'Gath carry threat: 6/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a directional leap that any knockup cancels — build the fight around landing it uncontested. Cho'Gath carry threat: 6/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

notes: Adopted the mirror's chart rather than the packet's, per the mirror rule. The most dangerous claim here was the level-6 spike telling you to ult 'through Rupture and Silence' — both of those cancel Infinite Duress, so the page was instructing the exact play that loses the fight. Also corrected the late-game framing: Feast stacking does NOT wall Warwick out, because Jaws of the Beast scales with the target's maximum health; Feral Scream is the real problem. Note for the user: chogath.json tags Rupture with a 'grounding' flag, which is a tooltip-parse misfire on the phrase 'Ruptures the ground' — I did not write grounding anywhere.
